demographics.trauma_type: Unexpected or traumatic death of a loved one

Triggers.value: Sleeping alone or in an unfamiliar place
A specific texture associated with the event

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Watching TV programmes/ films or reading about similar events
I dwell on how the event could have been prevented
perform mental rituals to prevent bad things from happening again

Threat.value: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

Negative Appraisals.value: Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore
I will not be able to control my anger and will do something terrible
I have failed in my most important role in life

issues.item: Triggers: Loss of Autonomy: Being forced to do something
issues.explanation: For traumatic bereavement, 'Loss of Autonomy' as a core trigger is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile. The other triggers (sleeping alone, specific texture) plausibly evoke absence/loss, but being forced to do something suggests a coercive/interpersonal threat context not otherwise represented in memory, appraisals, or strategies.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
issues.explanation: The threat items centered on sudden nearby movement and unexpected touch imply a strong physical-assault style danger response. In a profile for unexpected death of a loved one, this is difficult to integrate with the selected triggers and appraisals, which are focused more on loss, guilt, and meaning. Hypervigilance alone would fit high PTSD severity, but these specific startle contents are too skewed toward immediate interpersonal/physical threat.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Touch: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
issues.explanation: 'Fear of Rage' is not impossible after bereavement, but here it sits awkwardly with the rest of the profile because there are no complementary items suggesting anger-based triggers, aggressive urges, conflict, or strategies to manage anger. It pulls the profile toward a different formulation than the other appraisal items ('Lost Meaning', 'Failed Role'), which fit traumatic loss much better.

issues.item: Triggers: Loss of Autonomy: Being forced to do something
issues.explanation: The trigger set is difficult to reconcile with the trauma type of unexpected death of a loved one. 'Loss of autonomy,' 'sleeping alone/unfamiliar place,' and a specific tactile texture suggest a threat context involving coercion, assault, captivity, hospitalisation, or displacement, which is not reflected elsewhere in the profile and is hard to connect to bereavement trauma.

issues.item: Triggers: Sleeping Alone: Sleeping alone or in an unfamiliar place
issues.explanation: Threat items are dominated by physical-danger responses to nearby movement and unexpected touch. For a loved-one death trauma, these can occur, but here they imply a bodily/interpersonal danger template that is not supported by the listed triggers, appraisals, or memory content, making the profile clinically incoherent.

issues.item: Triggers: Tactile (Texture): A specific texture associated with the event
issues.explanation: 'Fear of rage' implies concern about losing control and harming others, but the rest of the profile centers on bereavement-related guilt, meaninglessness, avoidance of reminders, and prevention rumination. Without corroborating anger, aggression, or interpersonal-conflict content elsewhere, this appraisal pulls in a different syndrome picture and is hard to explain as part of the same formulation.

issues.item: Triggers: Loss of Autonomy: Being forced to do something
issues.explanation: For traumatic bereavement, the trigger 'being forced to do something' is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile. The other triggers and strategies center on reminders of loss and separation, but this item implies a coercion/control theme that is not reflected elsewhere in threat, memory, or appraisals.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
issues.explanation: The threat items focused on sudden movement and unexpected touch suggest a trauma organized around interpersonal or physical assault danger. In this bereavement profile, other items emphasize grief, guilt, and prevention-focused rumination rather than bodily attack, so these threat items are difficult to explain clinically as part of the same formulation.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Touch: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
issues.explanation: 'Fear of Rage' is not well supported by the rest of the profile. No other items indicate anger, aggression, conflict, or behavioral dyscontrol; the appraisals otherwise center on loss of meaning and failed role after a loved one's death. This item pulls toward a different clinical theme than the remainder of the self-report.

issues.item: Triggers: Loss of Autonomy: Being forced to do something
issues.explanation: For trauma type of unexpected death of a loved one, 'Loss of Autonomy/being forced to do something' is a weakly fitting trigger unless there is additional trauma context involving coercion or restraint; it does not cohere well with the rest of the profile, which centers on bereavement, guilt, and prevention-focused coping.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
issues.explanation: The threat profile is dominated by physically imminent danger cues (movement nearby, unexpected touch, hypervigilance), which is more characteristic of assault/combat-type trauma than traumatic bereavement. In this profile there are no memory items or appraisals linking the death to interpersonal attack or bodily threat, so these items do not connect well to the stated trauma type.

issues.item: Triggers: Loss of Autonomy: Being forced to do something
issues.explanation: The trauma type is unexpected death of a loved one, but 'being forced to do something' is a trigger more typical of interpersonal coercion, captivity, or assault. It is hard to connect this trigger coherently to the rest of this bereavement-focused profile.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
issues.explanation: The threat items center on physical danger cues from nearby movement/touch, which fits assault-type trauma more than traumatic bereavement. With no corresponding memory content or appraisal themes about bodily attack, these threat reactions are difficult to explain clinically in this profile.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Touch: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
issues.explanation: The appraisal 'I will not be able to control my anger and will do something terrible' introduces a perpetration/violence-control theme that is not supported by the triggers, trauma type, or other appraisals. It sits awkwardly beside grief/failure/meaning-loss themes and is hard to integrate into a single formulation.

issues.item: Triggers: Loss of Autonomy: Being forced to do something
issues.explanation: The trigger pattern is weakly matched to the trauma type of unexpected death of a loved one. 'Loss of Autonomy/being forced to do something' is more characteristic of assault, captivity, or coercive trauma than bereavement-related PTSD, and it does not fit well with the other listed triggers.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Movement: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
issues.explanation: The threat items emphasize a bodily-interpersonal danger state ('unexpected movement nearby', 'unexpected touch') that suggests fear of immediate physical attack. For traumatic bereavement this is hard to reconcile unless the death involved personal physical threat, which is not indicated by the trauma type or the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Threat: Startle to Touch: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
issues.explanation: 'Fear of Rage' is not impossible after bereavement, but in this profile it pulls toward fear of losing control and harming others, which is not well supported by the trigger set, threat set, or strategies. The rest of the appraisals center on loss, meaning, and failed role; this item introduces a different problem theme without clear linkage.
